questions.q: How many row-level formulas can a single report contain?
questions.explain: A report can have exactly one row-level formula, and it can reference at most five fields.

questions.q: What's the key difference between a row-level formula and a summary formula?
options: Row-level formulas only work on currency fields
A row-level formula calculates once per record; a summary formula calculates once per group or for the report
Summary formulas can only be used in Tabular reports
questions.explain: Row-level formulas run per individual record, like a formula field would. Summary formulas run per group (or report-wide if ungrouped), not per row.

questions.q: A summary formula is written as WON:SUM / CLOSED:SUM to calculate a win rate. What does this represent?
options: The count of won opportunities divided by the count of all opportunities
The sum of won-opportunity amounts divided by the sum of closed-opportunity amounts
A row-level comparison between two fields on one record
questions.explain: Each operand references a summarized (aggregated) field, in this case the Sum of a Won column divided by the Sum of a Closed column, producing one ratio per group.

questions.q: Which function would you use to show a group's value as a percentage of its parent group's total?
questions.explain: PARENTGROUPVAL returns a summarized value from an outer (parent) grouping level, which is exactly what a "percent of total" formula needs to divide against.

questions.q: Before applying a new report formula, what should you always do?
options: Export the report to CSV first
Click Validate to catch type mismatches or syntax errors
Switch the report to Tabular format
questions.explain: The formula editor's Validate button checks the formula for problems like type mismatches before you commit it with Apply.
